rows.text: The earthworm's working systems complete its anatomy. rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Septal: segment 15 onward, nephrostome, enteronephric.
Integumentary: all but the first two segments, no funnel, exonephric.
Pharyngeal: segments 4, 5, 6, no funnel, enteronephric.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Enteronephric ducts open into the gut. Exonephric ducts open on the skin. Septal nephridia are enteronephric. Integumentary nephridia are exonephric.  ·  Integumentary and pharyngeal nephridia have no nephrostome. Only septal nephridia collect coelomic fluid through a ciliated funnel.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Do not give every nephridium a nephrostome. That mistake collapses the three types into one.  ·  Supra-intestinal ducts are part of the septal system. They are not a fourth kind of nephridium.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Septal nephridium*** — the standard nephridium anatomy with nephrostome and twisted lobe.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Reproductive organs, copulation and the cocoon are the next note.  ·  The segment numbers are those of Pheretima posthuma.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Make a three-row table: type, segments, funnel or not, where the duct opens.  ·  Write the reflex as five numbered steps.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Septal into gut, integumentary to skin, pharyngeal to mouth."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** How many spermathecae does Pheretima have and where? **Answer.** **Four pairs**, located in **segments 6–9** (i.e. in the intersegmental grooves of 5/6, 6/7, 7/8, 8/9). Each spermatheca **stores the partner's sperm** received during copulation, releasing it later to fertilise the ova as the cocoon is formed.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Enteronephric excretion conserves water:** excreting into the gut lets the worm reabsorb water and salts — a soil adaptation; integumentary nephridia handle the exonephric route.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Nephridia types: septal (septa from 15, enteronephric, nephrostome + twisted lobe, 40–50/segment), integumentary (body wall, exonephric, all segments except first two), pharyngeal (tufts in 4, 5, 6, ducts to pharynx).  ·  Septal nephridium: nephrostome → neck → short straight lobe + long twisted lobe (4 loops) → septal excretory duct → intestine; excretes hypotonic urine, conserves salts.  ·  Nervous: dorsal supra-pharyngeal ganglia (3) + sub-pharyngeal ganglia (4) + double ventral nerve cord with segmental ganglia; photoreceptors, no eyes.  ·  Reproductive: hermaphrodite; testes 10, 11; seminal vesicles 9, 12; prostate glands + male pores 18; ovaries 13, female pore 14, four pairs spermathecae 6–9; cross-fertilisation; cocoon from clitellum mucus, direct development.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Earthworm urine is hypotonic — the nephridia reabsorb salts before excreting, an adaptation to soil life.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Septal nephridia of Pheretima → B  ·  Pharyngeal nephridia lie in segments → A

rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Worm's Working Systems Completing the earthworm anatomy: the **excretory system of nephridia** (with the septal nephridia in detail), the **central nervous system** of a double ventral nerve cord with ganglia, and the **reproductive system** of a simultaneous hermaphrodite that still cross-fertilises.  ·  ## 2. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Ganglia: cerebral in 3, sub-pharyngeal in 4, then one ganglion per segment.  ·  The earthworm's nerve cord is ventral and solid. The frog's is dorsal and hollow. 'Nerve cord' alone is not a shared structure.  ·  The brain is the supra-pharyngeal ganglia in segment 3, not a swelling of the ventral cord in the clitellum.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Segment numbers again: nephridia types are located by segment — septal from 15, pharyngeal in 4–6.  ·  "A hermaphrodite that still crosses: the worm's compromise between scarcity and dispersal."  ·  Why does a hermaphrodite animal still cross-fertilise? **Answer.** Because **self-fertilisation is genetic suicide in the long run**: mating with another individual recombines genes, restores heterozygosity, masks deleterious recessives and keeps the population adaptable.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 3. Nervous System - **Central nervous system:** a **ventral nerve cord** (double) running from segment 4 to the last, with a **ganglion in each segment**; anteriorly it divides around the pharynx into a circumpharyngeal ring with a **dorsal "brain" (supra-pharyngeal ganglia)** in segment 3 and **sub-pharyngeal…  ·  **Nephridia types — the three-way classification** | Type | Where found | Opens into | Function note | |---|---|---|---| | Septal | Behind each septum from 15th segment | Intestine (enteronephric) | Most numerous; water conservation | | Pharyngeal | Pharyngeal region (4-6 segments) | Pharynx/buccal cavity | Also…  ·  ## 4. Reproductive System Pheretima is a **simultaneous hermaphrodite** but practises **cross-fertilisation** by copulation. **Male organs:** - **Two testes** in segments 10 and 11, with **testis sacs**. - **Two seminal vesicles** in segments 9 and 12 — store and mature sperm.…
